name: Fuerte de Carchuna and the Motril front, Granada coast
story: After the fall of Málaga the front on the Granada coast stabilised between Motril (Nationalist) and the Republican zone to the east, and stayed there until 1939. On 23 May 1938 a Republican guerrilla unit landed by boat and attacked the fort of Carchuna, where prisoners (mostly Asturian miners) were held as forced labourers; 308 escaped to the Republican lines. It was one of the most successful special operations of the war. Trenches of the static front survive nearby.
see: The 18th-century coastal fort of Carchuna and remains of the front-line trenches.
plan: The fort houses a free interpretation centre (weekdays, see Visiting); trenches on the nearby hills — ask locally.
